hello.note: The first в is silent: zdrastvuyte. Casual: Привет (privet).

goodbye.note: Said almost as one word: dasvidanya. Casual: Пока (poka).

please.note: Also answers a thank-you and means 'here you are'. Often said pozhalsta.

youre_welcome.note: Stress on ne; что sounds like shto. Also very common: Пожалуйста (pozhaluysta).

sorry.note: Casual: Извини (izvini). More formal: Прошу прощения (proshu proshcheniya).

excuse_me.note: Извините (izvinite) works just as well. Both also mean 'sorry'.

how_are_you.note: Casual: Как дела? (kak dela?). Expect an honest answer, not just 'fine'.

im_fine.note: Very common and more modest: Нормально (normalno), 'OK'.

whats_your_name.note: Casual: Как тебя зовут? (kak tebya zovut?)

my_name_is.note: Literally 'they call me …'. Or simply: Я … (ya …).

im_from.note: The country changes its ending: из России (iz Rossii), из Америки (iz Ameriki).

dont_understand.note: To ask for a repeat: Повторите, пожалуйста (povtorite, pozhaluysta).

where.note: For 'where to?': Куда? (kuda?). For 'where from?': Откуда? (otkuda?)

how_much.note: When pointing at something, just: Сколько? (skolko?)

where_bathroom.note: Toilet doors are often marked М (men) and Ж (women).

can_you_help.note: Softer: Вы не могли бы мне помочь? (vy ne mogli by mne pomoch?)

what_time.note: Also very common: Сколько времени? (skolko vremeni?)

one.note: With feminine nouns: одна (odna); neuter: одно (odno). Counting aloud: раз (raz).

five.note: From five on, nouns take the genitive plural: пять рублей (pyat rubley).

water.note: Still: без газа (bez gaza). Sparkling: с газом (s gazom).

coffee.note: Never changes its ending, and is traditionally treated as masculine.

bread.note: The final б sounds like p: khlep.

im_hungry.note: Literally 'I want to eat'. Also: Я голоден (ya goloden); a woman says: Я голодна (ya golodna).

menu_please.note: Stress on the last syllable of меню, which never changes its ending.

bill_please.note: Сч sounds like a long soft sh. Also very common: Можно счёт? (mozhno schyot?)

delicious.note: To thank a host after the meal: Было очень вкусно! (bylo ochen vkusno!)

no_meat.note: I'm vegetarian: Я вегетарианец (ya vegetarianets); a woman says: Я вегетарианка (ya vegetarianka).

enjoy_meal.note: The г in -ого is said v: priyatnovo. Often just Приятного! (priyatnogo!)

left.note: For where something is: слева (sleva), on the left.

right.note: For where something is: справа (sprava), on the right.

airport.note: To the airport: в аэропорт (v aeroport).

hotel.note: Отель (otel) is also common, especially for upscale hotels.

train_station.note: A city's railway station. A metro station is станция (stantsiya).

want_to_go.note: Some places take на, not в: на вокзал (na vokzal). Literal: Я хочу поехать в … (ya khochu poyekhat v …).

cheaper.note: Casual: А подешевле нет? (a podeshevle net?)

id_like_this.note: When buying: Я возьму это (ya vozmu eto), 'I'll take this'.

just_looking.note: Often the answer to Вам помочь? (vam pomoch?), 'Can I help you?'.

pay_card.note: Short and very common: Можно картой? (mozhno kartoy?)

cash.note: The answer to 'card or cash?'. Cash itself is наличные (nalichnyye), casually наличка (nalichka).

closed.note: Also on doors: Перерыв (pereryv), closed for a break.

today.note: The г is said v: sevodnya.

now.note: Also 'in a moment': Сейчас! means 'Coming!'. In fast speech it sounds like shchas.

later.note: The зж is one long zh sound, with no separate z. Just as common: потом (potom), 'afterwards'.

good_night.note: Wishes a good sleep. When leaving late in the evening: Доброй ночи (dobroy nochi).

call_police.note: In Russia, 112 reaches all emergency services.

need_doctor.note: Call an ambulance: Вызовите скорую! (vyzovite skoruyu!)

im_lost.note: A woman says: Я заблудилась (ya zabludilas).

dont_feel_well.note: The first в is silent: chustvuyu. Sudden and serious: Мне плохо (mne plokho).

lost_phone.note: A woman says: Я потеряла телефон (ya poteryala telefon).

allergic.note: A final -а becomes -у, -я becomes -ю: на рыбу (na rybu), to fish.

be_careful.note: As parting advice: Будьте осторожны! (budte ostorozhny!)

no_problem.note: After an apology: Ничего страшного (nichego strashnogo), 'no harm done'.

of_course.note: The чн is said shn: koneshno.

i_like_it.note: Built as 'it pleases me', so the thing liked is the subject: Мне нравится чай (mne nravitsya chay).

im_tired.note: A woman says: Я устала (ya ustala).

im_happy.note: A woman says: Я счастлива (ya schastliva). The т is silent. 'Glad': рад, a woman рада (rad, rada).

welcome.note: At the door you will also hear Проходите! (prokhodite!), 'come in!'.

mother.note: The everyday word, even among adults. More formal: мать (mat).

father.note: The everyday word, even among adults. More formal: отец (otets).

brother.note: Older brother: старший брат (starshiy brat); younger: младший (mladshiy).

child.note: Plural: дети (deti). Son: сын (syn); daughter: дочь (doch).

friend.note: A female friend: подруга (podruga). The final г sounds like k: druk.

this_is_my_friend.note: For a female friend: Это моя подруга (eto moya podruga).

are_you_married.note: To a woman: Вы замужем? (vy zamuzhem?)

have_children.note: Casual: У тебя есть дети? (u tebya yest deti?)

monday.note: Days are not capitalised in Russian. On Monday: в понедельник (v ponedelnik).

tuesday.note: From второй (vtoroy), 'second'. On Tuesday: во вторник (vo vtornik), with во, not в.

wednesday.note: Literally 'middle', the middle of the week. On Wednesday: в среду (v sredu).

thursday.note: From четвёртый (chetvyortyy), 'fourth'. The final г sounds like k: chetverk.

friday.note: From пятый (pyatyy), 'fifth'. On Friday: в пятницу (v pyatnitsu).

sunday.note: Literally 'resurrection'. On Sunday: в воскресенье (v voskresenye).

weekend.note: Literally 'days off'. At the weekend: на выходных (na vykhodnykh).

what_day.note: For the date: Какое сегодня число? (kakoye segodnya chislo?)

next_week.note: Last week: на прошлой неделе (na proshloy nedele).

eleven.note: The д is silent: odinatsat. All the teens end in -надцать (-nadtsat), 'on ten'.

twelve.note: Built on две (dve), not два: 'two on ten'.

twenty.note: Literally 'two tens'. The д before ц is silent: dvatsat.

thirty.note: Literally 'three tens'. Forty is irregular: сорок (sorok).

fifty.note: Literally 'five tens', stressed at the end. 60–80 are built the same way; 70 and 80 stress the start.

hundred.note: Two hundred: двести (dvesti); five hundred: пятьсот (pyatsot).

thousand.note: Two thousand: две тысячи (dve tysyachi); five thousand: пять тысяч (pyat tysyach).

how_old.note: Casual: Сколько тебе лет? (skolko tebe let?)

years_old.note: Лет (let) after most numbers; год (god) after 1, 21, 31…; года (goda) after 2–4, 22–24…

blue.note: Dark blue. Light or sky blue counts as a separate colour: голубой (goluboy).

green.note: The ё is always stressed and said yo, even when printed as е.

what_colour.note: The г in -ого is said v: kakovo.

this_one.note: Agrees with the item: эта (eta) for feminine, это (eto) for neuter nouns.

that_one.note: Вон means 'over there'. Feminine: та (ta); neuter: то (to).

another_one.note: For feminine nouns: ещё одну (yeshchyo odnu). For a round of drinks: Повторите! (povtorite!)

its_raining.note: Literally 'rain is going'. It's snowing: Идёт снег (idyot sneg).

its_sunny.note: Also: Светит солнце (svetit solntse), 'the sun is shining'. The л in солнце is silent.

its_windy.note: Also: Дует ветер (duyet veter), 'the wind is blowing'.

umbrella.note: The diminutive зонтик (zontik) is just as common.

have_reservation.note: Shorter and very common: У меня бронь (u menya bron).

room.note: A hotel room is номер; a room in a home is комната (komnata).

passport.note: Russians call their travel passport загранпаспорт (zagranpasport).

luggage.note: Your bags are often just вещи (veshchi), 'things'. Suitcase: чемодан (chemodan).

wifi_password.note: Often written Wi-Fi, but always said vay-fay.

check_out_time.note: Literally 'when must I free the room?'. Hotels call check-out time расчётный час (raschyotnyy chas).

map.note: Also means a bank card. City map: карта города (karta goroda).

next_train.note: A suburban commuter train is электричка (elektrichka).

is_this_seat_free.note: Also very common: Здесь не занято? (zdes ne zanyato?), 'Is this taken?'

what_do_you_do.note: Broader, covering studies too: Чем вы занимаетесь? (chem vy zanimayetes?)

i_work_in.note: The ending changes: в банке (v banke), в школе (v shkole). Some places take на: на заводе (na zavode).

im_student.note: A woman says: Я студентка (ya studentka).

meeting.note: A meeting with a client or partner: встреча (vstrecha).

im_busy.note: A woman says: Я занята (ya zanyata).

day_off.note: I'm off today: У меня сегодня выходной (u menya segodnya vykhodnoy).

colleague.note: Same word for a woman, but it then takes feminine words: моя коллега (moya kollega).

lets_start.note: Among friends: Давай начнём (davay nachnyom). Or just: Начнём! (nachnyom!)

good_job.note: Very common: Молодец! (molodets!), 'well done!', to a man or a woman.

table_for_two.note: For three: на троих (na troikh); for four: на четверых (na chetverykh).

what_recommend.note: Also: Что вы порекомендуете? (chto vy porekomenduyete?)

not_spicy.note: Agrees with блюдо (blyudo), 'dish'. With a masculine dish like суп (sup): не острый (ne ostryy).

vegetarian_food.note: Asking for it: У вас есть вегетарианские блюда? (u vas yest vegetarianskiye blyuda?)

more_water.note: Воды is the 'some water' form of вода (voda).

im_full.note: A woman says: Я наелась (ya nayelas).

takeaway.note: You may be asked: Здесь или с собой? (zdes ili s soboy?), 'for here or to go?'

it_was_delicious.note: To thank a host: Спасибо, всё было очень вкусно! (spasibo, vsyo bylo ochen vkusno!)

keep_change.note: Literally 'no change needed'. The change itself is сдача (sdacha).

stomach.note: The belly, where it hurts. The organ itself is желудок (zheludok).

head_hurts.note: Same pattern for any body part: У меня болит живот (u menya bolit zhivot).

have_fever.note: Literally 'I have a temperature'. High fever: высокая температура (vysokaya temperatura).

medicine.note: Medicine for a cough: лекарство от кашля (lekarstvo ot kashlya).

call_ambulance.note: Short for скорая помощь (skoraya pomoshch). In Russia, 103 calls an ambulance; 112 also works.

dentist.note: Everyday alternative: зубной врач (zubnoy vrach), 'tooth doctor'.

feel_better.note: Often with уже, 'already': Мне уже лучше (mne uzhe luchshe). Лучше is said lutshe.

get_well.note: To a friend: Поправляйся! (popravlyaysya!) In writing: Скорейшего выздоровления! (skoreyshego vyzdorovleniya!)

lets_meet.note: To a friend: Давай встретимся (davay vstretimsya).

are_you_free.note: Casual: Ты завтра свободен? (ty zavtra svoboden?); to a woman: свободна (svobodna).

call_me.note: Casual: Позвони мне (pozvoni mne). Text me: Напишите мне (napishite mne).

your_number.note: Casual: Какой у тебя номер? (kakoy u tebya nomer?)

see_you_soon.note: The г is said v: do skorovo. Also: Скоро увидимся! (skoro uvidimsya!)

have_nice_day.note: The г is said v: khoroshevo. In the evening: Хорошего вечера! (khoroshego vechera!)

good_luck.note: Before an exam: Ни пуха ни пера! (ni pukha ni pera!), answered with К чёрту! (k chyortu!)

happy_birthday.note: Never say it early: wishing it before the day is thought to bring bad luck.

thanks_a_lot.note: Just as common the other way round: Спасибо большое (spasibo bolshoye).

miss_you.note: Short and common: Скучаю! (skuchayu!) To several people: по вам (po vam).
